entries.description: enable backend sampling (experimental) (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_BACKEND_SAMPLING)
entries.notes: b10621 asks for the sampler to run on the compute backend instead of the CPU. mlxcel's sampler is always MLX ops on the accelerator, so the flag's only position describes what mlxcel already does and it is accepted as inert. There is no `--no-backend-sampling` to reject. Its environment variable is bound at runtime rather than through clap: b10621 fires a value-less option from the environment only for `on`/`enabled`/`true`/`1` (`common_arg_utils::is_truthy`), while clap's boolish parser accepts a wider vocabulary and errors outside it. llama.cpp writes this option with a single dash and several letters, which clap reads as a cluster of one-letter shorts; the argv pre-pass in `src/cli/llama_short_flags.rs` rewrites the exact upstream tokens to the long spelling before clap sees them. The flag-surface dump the manifest gate reads is long-spelling-only, so `accepted_spellings` records the long form; `tests/llama_ggml_runtime_cli.rs::every_b10621_short_spelling_reaches_its_own_option` covers the short ones.
divergence: Always on, where b10621 defaults it off and treats it as experimental; the flag cannot select the CPU sampler because mlxcel has none.

entries.description: KV cache data type for K allowed values: f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q5_1 (default: f16) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_TYPE_K)
entries.notes: The two vocabularies overlap on exactly one spelling. `f16` names the same thing on both sides, unquantized half-precision KV storage, so it is aliased onto mlxcel's `KVCacheMode::Fp16` and is the only b10621 value accepted. Every other GGML name is a different quantizer, not a different name for the same one: `q8_0` is block-wise with a per-block scale, mlxcel's `int8` is per-token absmax, and the Turbo modes are PolarQuant with a Walsh-Hadamard rotation. #1445 deliberately does not map `q8_0`/`q4_0`/`q4_1`/`iq4_nl`/`q5_0`/`q5_1` (and refuses `f32`/`bf16` for a different reason: they are unquantized GGML float types and mlxcel's KV cache has no f32 or bf16 storage to select, which the diagnostic says in its own sentence rather than calling them quantizers) onto any of them, because no numerical or storage equivalence has been demonstrated and naming similarity is not evidence; a mapping would leave a deployment believing its cache arithmetic is something it is not. Each of those values is rejected at startup with a diagnostic naming the value, why the vocabularies do not carry over, and the mlxcel modes that do exist. mlxcel's own `int8`, `fp16+turbo4`, `fp16+turbo3`, `turbo4` and `turbo4-delegated` remain available on the same flag and stay visible in `--help`; see docs/turbo-kv-cache.md. llama.cpp writes this option with a single dash and several letters, which clap reads as a cluster of one-letter shorts; the argv pre-pass in `src/cli/llama_short_flags.rs` rewrites the exact upstream tokens to the long spelling before clap sees them. The flag-surface dump the manifest gate reads is long-spelling-only, so `accepted_spellings` records the long form; `tests/llama_ggml_runtime_cli.rs::every_b10621_short_spelling_reaches_its_own_option` covers the short ones.
divergence: Value domain differs: of b10621's `f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q4_0, q4_1, iq4_nl, q5_0, q5_1` only `f16` is accepted; the rest are rejected rather than mapped onto a different quantizer.
mlxcel accepts additional values b10621 does not (`int8`, `fp16+turbo4`, `fp16+turbo3`, `turbo4`, `turbo4-delegated`).
